Let
\[
\phi_\tau(x)=\frac12x^TA_\tau x+b^Tx.
\]
For a trust-region minimizer there is a multiplier \(s\ge0\) such that
\[
(A_\tau+sI)x=-b,\qquad A_\tau+sI\succeq0,\qquad s(\|x\|^2-1)=0.
\]
Non-uniqueness can only occur in the hard case: \(A_\tau+sI\) is singular positive semidefinite, \(b\) is orthogonal to its nullspace, and the affine solution set of \((A_\tau+sI)x=-b\) meets the unit sphere in more than one point.

Since \(\lambda_{\min}(A_\tau)\le -3\), the singular hard-case shift satisfies \(s\ge3\). Put
\[
M=A_\tau+sI.
\]
A null vector \(y\) of \(M\) must satisfy, after setting \(y_1=1\),
\[
y=\left(1,\ 3-s,\ s^2-3s-1,\ -\frac{s^2-3s-1}{s+4}\right).
\]
The range condition \(b\perp y\) gives
\[
1+3(3-s)+(s^2-3s-1)-\frac{3(s^2-3s-1)}{s+4}=0,
\]
equivalently
\[
g(s):=s^3-5s^2-6s+39=0.
\]
The cubic has exactly two roots with \(s\ge3\): one in \((17/5,24/7)\) and one in \((4,9/2)\).

For such an \(s\), the third row of \(My=0\) determines
\[
\tau=\frac{s-3}{s^2-3s-1}+\frac1{s+4}-s.
\]
Eliminating \(s\) from this relation and \(g(s)=0\) gives
\[
f(\tau):=81\tau^3+254\tau^2-793\tau-2197=0.
\]
The two corresponding \(\tau\)-values in \([-4,-2]\) are the roots of \(f\) in
\[
(-39/10,-19/5)\quad\text{and}\quad(-12/5,-23/10).
\]

It remains to test the unit boundary condition. Solving \(Mx=-b\), every solution has the form
\[
x=c+ay,\qquad
c=\left(0,-1,s-3,-\frac{s}{s+4}\right).
\]
The minimum possible squared norm among these solutions is
\[
\|c\|^2-\frac{(c\cdot y)^2}{\|y\|^2}.
\]
A direct reduction using \(g(s)=0\) shows that
\[
\left(\|c\|^2-\frac{(c\cdot y)^2}{\|y\|^2}\right)-1
\]
has the same sign as
\[
R(s)=-7029s^2+4755s+66360.
\]
For the smaller positive root \(s\in(17/5,24/7)\), \(R(s)>0\), so every solution of \(Mx=-b\) has norm \(>1\). Thus that candidate does not produce a trust-region minimizer.

For the larger positive root \(s\in(4,9/2)\), \(R(s)<0\), so the minimum-norm solution has norm \(<1\). Since \(\ker M=\mathbb R y\) is one-dimensional, the equation
\[
\|c+ay\|=1
\]
has exactly two real solutions for \(a\). Both satisfy the KKT conditions with \(M\succeq0\), hence both are global minimizers. Therefore \(\mathcal X_\tau\) is non-singleton for exactly one parameter.

\[
\boxed{\tau_*=\operatorname{root}_{(-39/10,-19/5)}\!\left(81x^3+254x^2-793x-2197\right)}
\]
